conviction_note: Sum of four signed findings (+5.0, +1.5, +1.0, -2.0): the externally observable demand proxy for SPWH's exact fiscal Q2 window (May 3 - Aug 1 2026) accelerated to roughly +7.7% YoY from ~+2 to +3% in fiscal Q1, and both of the strong months landed AFTER management set the FY guide on 2 June and after the last analyst revision cycle, against a consensus that still has revenue flat; sized well below the 14.1% historical median because the same demand arrives in SPWH's lowest-gross-margin category and because there is no option chain to confirm what is priced.

findings.finding: NSSF-adjusted NICS background checks for the three calendar months that are SPWH's fiscal Q2 (quarter ends 1 Aug 2026) ran May +3.2% (1,105,758), June +11.7% (1,123,006) and July +8.5% (1,061,883) YoY -- roughly +7.7% for the quarter -- versus only +3.5% (Feb) and +1.9% (Mar) in the fiscal Q1 in which SPWH delivered +2.1% same-store sales and +6.3% hunting/shooting; the two strongest months were published on 6 July and 5 August, after management reaffirmed FY comps of -1.0% to +2.0% on 2 June with visibility only through soft May.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-06 (publication date stated on page; URL path /2026/07/)
findings.why_not_priced: A 30 Aug 2026 preview states the market expects SPWH revenue 'flat year on year' and that analysts have 'generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days' -- i.e. the three estimates did not move after the 6 July (+11.7%) and 5 August (+8.5%) NICS releases (https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/sportsmans-warehouse-earnings-look-spwh-030052393.html, dated 2026-08-30 in the document). If it were priced the estimate revision breadth would be positive, the FY comp guide would already be treated as stale, and the stock would not be sitting 5.8% above its 52-week low with a +3.0% 20-day run-up a month after Ruger disclosed +19% retail sell-through. On top of that, no US outdoor peer has yet reported this window: Academy does not report fiscal Q2 until 9 September 2026 (https://investors.academy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/academy-sports-outdoors-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-2026), so SPWH prints first and there is no peer datapoint in the tape.
findings.independence: Two different source classes point the same way and neither is a background-check statistic. (1) Sturm Ruger, 29 July 2026: net sales +19%, estimated sell-through from distributors to retailers +19% versus 'a 5% increase in adjusted NICS', with distributor inventories DOWN 45,800 units and factory finished goods down 100,100 units -- that is SPWH's own inbound channel destocking on retail pull-through (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results, date in URL path 20260729). (2) Olin's Winchester segment Q2 2026: sales +11.8% to $500.3m on higher commercial ammunition volume AND price, with tariffs reducing import competition, and management guiding to sequential improvement into the fall hunting season (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/olin-oln-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/, date in URL path 2026/08/07). NOTE ON OVERLAP: these are corroboration for this one finding, not separate findings -- they measure the same underlying demand acceleration and are folded into this single +5.0, deliberately not counted twice.

findings.finding: The $200 NFA transfer tax on suppressors fell to $0 on 1 January 2026, and NFA background checks have roughly doubled-to-tripled in SPWH's fiscal Q2 window (May 2026 146,551 vs 73,138, +100.4%; June 2026 166,677 vs 60,147, +177.1%; July 2026 130,013, +108.8%) -- and SPWH has been selling suppressors online through a 'Delivered by Silencer Central' drop-ship partnership since 12 March 2025, yet the words suppressor, silencer and NFA do not appear anywhere on its Q1 2026 earnings call.
findings.source_date: 2025-03-12 (date in URL path /2025/03/12/ -- deliberately checked, this is a 2025 release and predates the tax change)
findings.why_not_priced: There is no sell-side model line for this: the category is not in SPWH's reported department disclosure, was never quantified on a call, and is not mentioned in the 30 Aug preview. If it were priced, at least one of the three estimates would have been raised off it, and the 'weak outdoor retail' framing in the wire copy would instead read as a new-category story. The check on whether the category is worth anything at retail is not SPWH's own words but Academy's: on its 10 June 2026 call Academy said suppressors were launched in a limited number of stores, are going to 100+ stores by year-end, and are '100% accretive as it is entirely new to the assortment, benefiting from recent changes in procurement laws'.
findings.independence: Academy Sports and Outdoors' Q1 2026 call on 10 June 2026 independently validates the category economics and the causal link to the law change: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/academy-sports-outdoors-inc-q1-123000366.html (article date 2026-06-10, stated in the document). The NFA check counts come from a different source again: https://www.ammoland.com/2026/08/july-2026-gun-sales-nics-nfa-checks-surge/ (date in URL path /2026/08/) and https://www.ammoland.com/2026/07/june-2026-nics-nfa-suppressor-checks-surge/ (/2026/07/). This is a distinct fact from finding 1 -- a statutory change and a new category, not a comp rate -- but I note the NFA check series and the NICS series are published by the same body, so a scorer collapsing NSSF releases into one cluster should treat this finding's residual as the Silencer Central channel and the Academy read, not the check counts.

findings.finding: The 8-K filed 24 June 2026 (event 18 June 2026) pushed BOTH the senior secured revolver (resized $350m to $315m) and the $45m ABL term loan out to 18 June 2031, removing the 27 May 2027 revolver maturity that was still disclosed in the Q1 10-Q alongside $114.6m of borrowing-base availability -- so the balance-sheet mechanism that produced this stock's two extreme prints (-29.8% on 4 Dec 2025, +97.9% on 1 Apr 2025) cannot recur in the same form at this print.
findings.why_not_priced: The fact is public and ten weeks old, so I am NOT claiming the extension itself is unpriced -- I am claiming its effect on the shape of this reaction is. The sealed baseline's 14.1% expected move is the median of eight prints, two of which (-29.8%, +97.9%) were refinancing/liquidity events under a facility that matured inside two years; with no maturity inside five years and $114.6m of availability, that left tail is structurally smaller here and the baseline number is mechanically too wide. If the market had re-underwritten the equity for a five-year runway the stock would not still be trading at $1.185 with a $45m market cap and a +3.0% 20-day run-up, i.e. still priced as a distressed option; that non-reaction is the observable evidence. The signed impact is small on purpose -- the content is a narrower distribution, not a direction.
findings.independence: The old 27 May 2027 maturity and the $114.6m availability come from the Q1 10-Q, a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000119312526253546/spwh-20260502.htm (period ended 2026-05-02, filed June 2026). The resizing rationale ('to better align the facility's size with current operating needs') is separately reported at https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:6792bc30e6cb1:0-sportsman-s-warehouse-refinances-abl-term-loan-to-2031-amends-revolver-with-wells-fargo/. I also confirmed from EDGAR that this is the ONLY 8-K SPWH has filed since 1 June 2026 -- no Nasdaq notice, no impairment, no pre-announcement.

findings.finding: The demand that is accelerating is SPWH's lowest-margin demand: Q1 2026 gross margin fell to 29.6% from 30.4% specifically because firearms and ammunition mix rose while higher-margin categories declined, Q1 adjusted EBITDA was -$8.1m against a full-year guide of $30-36m that is therefore entirely back-half-loaded, and Academy told investors on 10 June 2026 -- eight days after SPWH last spoke -- that it was 'tracking at flat comparable sales through the Memorial Day period' on 'persistent $4+ gas prices'.
findings.source_date: 2026-06-02 (Q1 FY2026 press release, thirteen weeks ended 2026-05-02, filed as 8-K Ex-99)
findings.why_not_priced: The gross margin mechanic is disclosed, so what is unpriced is its interaction with finding 1, not the fact itself: a NICS-led revenue beat can arrive with a lower gross margin rate and, with ~$148.4m of net debt carrying interest, still miss on EPS. If the market had worked this through, the coverage would frame a firearms-led beat as margin-dilutive rather than as good news, and the 30 Aug preview would not simply say 'revenue flat'. Academy's flat-through-Memorial-Day comment is the reason I do not extrapolate the whole +7.7% NICS quarter into comps -- the non-firearm half of the box (camp, apparel, footwear) is still fighting $4 gasoline.
findings.independence: The Academy datapoint is from a genuinely different entity and postdates SPWH's last public statement: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/academy-sports-outdoors-inc-q1-123000366.html (2026-06-10). SPWH's own Q1 language on 'continued consumer economic pressure and higher fuel prices' points the same way from the company's own release. OVERLAP DISCLOSED: this finding and finding 1 read the SAME underlying fact -- firearms/ammunition-led growth -- on opposite lines of the P&L (revenue vs gross margin rate). It is filed as a signed offset, not as independent negative evidence, and finding 1's +5.0 is already net of a gross-margin haircut; the two together are one thesis with an honest downside vent, not two theses. Finding 4 also shares the Q1 press release with the guidance and EBITDA figures cited in finding 1's supporting URLs.

baseline_tension: There is no 25-delta skew to agree or disagree with -- the chain has 23 contracts of total open interest and the baseline itself marks it unusable, so 'what is priced' here is inferred from a +3.0% 20-day run-up and 28.3% realised vol, which is a dead tape that has priced essentially no news, and my positive finding therefore cuts against nothing rather than fighting a positioned market; the one place I do cut against the baseline is magnitude, because its 14.1% median is inflated by two refinancing-era prints that the June 2031 maturity extension has taken off the table, so I expect a smaller-than-median move in the up direction.
